title: Shared Team AI Agent — Demo Authentication Iteration API
assumptions: This localhost MVP has one seeded consulting team, Northstar Consulting, with exactly three demo accounts: John, Mary, and Bob.
Authentication is demo-only: credentials are seeded in SQLite and passwords are stored as hashes. There is no account recovery, invitation, or SSO flow.

Successful login establishes a server-side session represented to the browser only by an HTTP-only, SameSite=Lax cookie with Path=/. Secure is enabled over HTTPS and may be disabled only for the localhost HTTP demo.
The server records last-seen time for the signed-in member. Shared memory persists team context, artifacts, and activity events.
Keyword matching is the MVP retrieval mechanism. The server may send bounded private history and relevant team-memory matches to the configured LLM provider.

authorization.session: Every /api endpoint except POST /api/auth/login and GET /api/health requires a valid, unexpired, unrevoked session cookie. Invalid session returns 401 without resource-existence details.
authorization.private_conversations: Server derives current user and team exclusively from the session. A member may list, read, create, and post only to conversations where user_id and team_id match their session. Cross-user or cross-team conversation IDs return 404.
authorization.shared_memory: Every authenticated member may search, read artifacts, and poll activity only for their own team. Clients do not submit team_id. Cross-team resources return 404.
authorization.shared_memory_writes: Server derives team_id and author_id from the session. Members may create their own team context and may patch only records they authored. Patching another member's item returns 403.

side_effects: creates or rotates a server-side session
sets the HTTP-only SameSite=Lax session cookie

endpoints.notes: conversations includes only the session user's conversations; users contains roster identity data without credentials.

endpoints.auth: session required; session team and author inferred
session required; author-only write within session team

behavior.login: A login accepts only seeded company email/password pairs. It returns identity metadata, never passwords, hashes, session IDs, or a credential list. Browser JavaScript relies on the HTTP-only cookie and calls GET /api/auth/me to resolve signed-in state.
behavior.logout: Logout revokes server-side session state, clears its cookie, and returns the browser to the public landing/login screen. Calling it with no valid session is safe.
behavior.duplicate_work: Every meaningful authenticated message searches only the session team's shared context before response generation. Related in-progress or complete work sets duplicate_resolution, identifies owner/status, returns saved artifacts, and recommends reuse or complementary work.
behavior.catch_up: POST /api/sessions returns shared events after the signed-in user's persisted previous_last_seen_at and then advances it. GET /api/activity with since supports subsequent polling.
behavior.authority: Facts, opinions, proposals, and decisions remain distinct. Only decisions may use confirmed status; competing proposals are never silently collapsed.
behavior.privacy: Private messages never become shared automatically. The agent may suggest a handoff, but the signed-in user must explicitly call POST /api/context. Shared data is accessible to John, Mary, and Bob only after login.
behavior.conversation_creation: POST /api/conversations creates an empty private conversation owned by the signed-in user. Missing titles receive a server-defined safe default; creation makes no shared context or activity event.
behavior.seeded_demo_scope: The database seeds John, Mary, and Bob as the only Northstar Consulting users. Demo credentials are implementation data and must be supplied separately in the local-demo handoff; no API exposes them.
